elements.content: Communication Goal: I can say who owns things.

Lesson overview:
- Level: A1 General English
- Unit: MODULE 4. HOME & EVERYDAY ENVIRONMENT
- Time: 60 min (Essential) / 90 min (Expanded) / 120 min (Full Workshop)
- Focus: Possessive 's
- Materials: vocabulary cards, audio, reading handout
Warm-up: say one word you already know for this topic.
Recycles possessive 's from Lesson 2.1.
Recycled language: mother, father, sister.
Answer from memory: which word belongs to this topic?
Which word belongs to this topic?
Core Active Vocabulary (10 items):

mother — the woman who is your parent. Example: This is my mother.
father — the man who is your parent. Example: My father works here.
sister — a girl or woman with the same parents as you. Example: This is my sister's bag.
brother — a boy or man with the same parents as you. Example: My brother's phone is new.
friend — a person you like and know well. Example: My friend's house is near.
teacher — a person who helps students learn. Example: My teacher's name is on the door.
name — the word people use for a person. Example: My teacher's name is Anna.
bag — a container you carry things in. Example: This is Marta's bag.
phone — a telephone. Example: Whose phone is this?
house — a building where a family lives. Example: My friend's house is near.
Essential Chunks & Functional Collocations:

• Whose ... is this?
• It is Marta's.
• My teacher's name is ...
• My friend's house ...
• It is not mine.
Vocabulary practice: choose the correct word.
Which word means 'the woman who is your parent'?
Which word means 'the man who is your parent'?
Complete the sentence with a word from the list.
The possessive 's is /s/, /z/ or /ɪz/.
Kate's /s/, Marta's /z/, George's /ɪz/
Listen and repeat three times.
Which word carries the main stress?
Grammar focus: Possessive ’s.
Add 's to a person to show possession: Marta's bag, my teacher's phone. Ask Whose bag is this? It is Marta's.
Controlled practice: choose the correct option.
Choose the correct sentence.
Choose the correct question.
Complete the sentence.
Reading: read the text and answer the questions.
This is Marta's bag. Her phone is in it and her keys are on the table. My teacher's name is on the door and my friend's house is near.
Listening: listen to the dialogue and answer the questions.
A: Whose phone is this? B: It is my sister's. A: And whose bag is that? B: It is Marta's bag.
Speaking: Pair and group tasks: Ask and answer Whose…? questions about everyday objects.

• Whose ... is this?
• It is Marta's.
• My teacher's name is ...
Writing: Write four to five sentences about "Ge A1 Possessive S" using the target grammar.
